```plato

//==
// # Function-valued fields
//
// A field that **stores a function value** rather than deriving its value from
// stored data. This is the compositional layer beneath the declarative node
// graphs of the next section: a function-valued field is built from a
// lambda, evaluated by invoking the stored function, and combined with another
// field into a new field holding the composed lambda. The combinators (Combine,
// MapValue, MapDomain, Union, Intersection, Difference, Offset) live in
// `fields-implicits.library.plato`, where a conversion named after each of these
// types lifts any field interface implementor into this form, implicitly, so the
// combinators apply to all of them.
//
// These are deliberately monomorphic (one type per domain/range pair) rather
// than one generic function-carrying type: the monomorphic shape is what
// monomorphizes cleanly to every backend.
//
// **Domain and range dimensions.** A IProcedural is classified by what it maps
// from and to; the dimension of the domain is the dimension of the form's
// parameter space, the dimension of the range is the space it lives in. The
// field interfaces of `fields.concepts.plato` are the point-domain rows of that
// table:
//
//   Number  -> Number    a scalar function of one variable (an easing curve)
//   Number  -> Point2D   a parametric curve in the plane
//   Number  -> Point3D   a parametric curve in space
//   Point2D -> Number    a planar scalar field (a 2D signed distance field)
//   Point2D -> Vector2D  a planar vector field
//   Point2D -> Point3D   a parametric surface in space
//   Point3D -> Number    a spatial scalar field (a 3D signed distance field)
//   Point3D -> Vector3D  a spatial vector field
//
// A IProcedural whose range is Boolean is a **predicate**: a threshold over a
// Number domain, a region over Point2D, a volume over Point3D — membership
// with no distance information (see `implicit-sdf.concepts.plato`). A
// IProcedural over an integer domain is a discrete field: an unbounded array, a
// texture sampler, or a voxel grid. Continuous forms are analytic and
// resolution independent; discrete forms (meshes, polylines, point clouds,
// sampled grids) instead enumerate a countable set of primitives.

// A planar scalar field defined by a stored function from a plane position to a
// number. The canonical function-valued field: heightmaps, masks, potentials,
// and planar signed distances all take this form.
type ScalarFunctionField2D
    implements IScalarField2D
{
    Function: Function1<Point2D, Number>;
}
```
